name: Scarlet AI Collective (Demo)
description: Explore machine learning through small, explainable projects, hands-on Python sessions, and discussion of how AI can help local communities. Members work in pairs, compare simple baselines, and examine model mistakes before presenting a result. This is a fictitious student organization for a product demonstration.
mission: Make practical AI learning approachable while treating evidence, data consent, and community impact as part of technical work.
eligibility: Open to students from any major; no AI or programming background is required. These are synthetic membership examples, not university policies.

faqs.question: When and where do you meet?
faqs.answer: Our sample meeting is Thursdays, 7:30–8:30 PM at Busch Student Center. The room and schedule are demonstration data; no real meeting is advertised.

faqs.question: How much does membership cost?
faqs.answer: The sample membership fee is Free. These are fictional dues, and this app does not collect payments.

faqs.question: Who can join, and do beginners need experience?
faqs.answer: Open to students from any major; no AI or programming background is required. Beginners are welcome, and sample activities include an introduction.

faqs.question: How do I join or contact the club?
faqs.answer: You can follow this demo organization in BetterGetInvolved to try the workflow. No actual membership is created. The example.org contact address is a placeholder and should not be used to contact a real organization.

faqs.question: Will I need a paid AI account or a powerful laptop?
faqs.answer: The demo curriculum uses small public or synthetic datasets and local Python tools. No paid AI account or powerful GPU is needed for the introductory activities.
